title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Eritrea: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Please accept sincere condolences for your loss. Eritrea does not operate public online civil-status, court, or legislative gazette portals (state site shabait.com publishes ministry news and policy statements only), so this guide cites verified international legal archives (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, Refworld, and HCCH) alongside accredited foreign consular guidance and Eritrean embassy websites. Because vital and judicial records cannot be requested remotely online, confirm current procedures directly with the relevant municipal administration or an Eritrean diplomatic mission.

steps.title: Obtain hospital medical papers and register the death across all local tiers
steps.html:
• Request the hospital-issued death certificate form (if the death occurred in a hospital) or a dead body certificate (if elsewhere), which Eritrean hospitals issue in both the local language (Tigrigna or Arabic) and English [1].
  • Register the death at the local Public Registration Office (which a local funeral director often assists with), and ensure family members or friends separately report the death to both the local Zoba Administration and sub-Zoba Administration [1][2].
  • Collect the full local certificate package: the official death certificate and an English translation issued by the Zoba Administration, a witness of death certificate issued by the Zoba Administration, and an acknowledgement letter issued by the sub-Zoba Administration [1].
  • Keep extra certified originals, because Eritrean embassies abroad (such as the Embassy of the State of Eritrea in London) do not issue civil death certificates and records in Eritrea must be obtained in person or via a local agent [8].

steps.title: Satisfy police clearance, burial or cremation rules, and repatriation permits
steps.html:
• If the cause of death is sudden, unnatural, violent, or unknown, local police and hospital physicians will initiate a post-mortem investigation before releasing the body [1].
  • Appoint a local funeral director to assemble the statutory clearance file needed for local burial, cremation, or export of remains: the Zoba certificate of death, witness of death certificate, sub-Zoba acknowledgement letter, a police clearance letter, an airport immigration police approval letter, and (for transport) an embalming certificate [1].
  • When shipping remains from abroad into Eritrea, missions such as the Embassy of the State of Eritrea in Washington, D.C. and the London Embassy require a legalized death certificate, non-contagious disease letters from a physician and health authority, an embalming certificate, coroner clearance for unnatural deaths, and proof of the deceased person's Eritrean nationality or Eritrean National ID (or verification by three Eritrean ID-holding witnesses) [8][9].

steps.title: Address estate succession, property claims, and court procedures
steps.html:
• Substantive succession and inheritance rights are governed by Book 3 (Successions) of the Civil Code of Eritrea (2015), which replaced the 1991 Transitional Civil Code and covers testate and intestate heirs, acceptance under benefit of inventory, and co-heir settlement [3].
  • Follow procedural filing rules under the Civil Procedure Code of Eritrea (2015) for estate petitions [5]; minor community-level disputes may be mediated or heard by elected local Community Courts, while formal inheritance decrees, contested property injunctions, and higher-value estates fall under regional Zoba Courts and the High Court [1][7].
  • If surviving relatives live outside Eritrea and cannot appear before Asmara notaries or regional courts, sign a detailed consular Power of Attorney naming a trusted representative in Eritrea [8][10].

steps.title: Check employment terminal pay, pensions, and Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare support
steps.html:
• Contact the deceased person's employer regarding accrued salary, final employment records, and work-related death compensation governed by Labour Proclamation No. 118/2001 [4].
  • Check whether the family qualifies for statutory allowances or rehabilitation programs administered by the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare, including ongoing financial disbursements for families of fallen martyrs established under Proclamation No. 137/2003 [6].
  • Where surviving relatives abroad must authorize a representative in Eritrea to collect pension or condolence-related entitlements, check dedicated embassy Power of Attorney categories [10].

steps.title: Complete non-Apostille consular legalization and Tigrigna, Arabic, or English translations
steps.html:
• Note that Eritrea is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so apostilles cannot replace diplomatic authentication and every cross-border document requires full consular legalization [11].
  • Original Eritrean death, Zoba, or court certificates intended for use abroad must first be stamped and signed by the Eritrean Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Asmara and then presented in original form to the receiving country's embassy or an accredited Eritrean mission [1][8].
  • Foreign-issued death certificates or court grants intended for use in Eritrea must first be authenticated by the issuing state's Foreign Ministry (such as the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office or the U.S. Department of State) before submission to the relevant Eritrean Embassy [2][8].

contacts.note: Provides appointment-only consular authentication of original legalized civil documents, Power of Attorney execution, and repatriation document verification.

contacts.note: Consular section handling Power of Attorney processing, National ID records, and shipment of remains permits (1708 New Hampshire Ave NW).

contacts.name: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
contacts.note: Publishes official guidance on Public Registration Office, Zoba Administration, sub-Zoba acknowledgement letters, and British Embassy Asmara liaison.

contacts.name: Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare
contacts.note: Administers welfare, rehabilitation, and Martyrs' family allowances under Proclamation No. 137/2003 (no public self-service online portal).
